transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you. Um, mostly I'm here because I'm just tired in a way that sleep doesn't seem to fix. It's gotten to the point where even basic things, like unloading the dishwasher or trying to read for my certificate class, just... they just feel like too much right now.
Aside from feeling exhausted, have you been feeling down, depressed, or sad?

Um, no, not really. I wouldn't say I feel sad or down. It's... it's more just this heavy feeling of being completely drained, you know? I don't feel like crying or anything like that. Just really, really tired.
{"intent": "Assess for post-exertional malaise to evaluate for chronic fatigue syndrome", "question": "Do you notice that your exhaustion becomes significantly worse after physical

Um, no, I haven't really noticed that. It's pretty much the same no matter what I do. Like, whether I'm just sitting on the couch or if I actually try to get up and do things, the tiredness is just constant. It doesn't really get worse just because I was moving around or doing something physical.
Have you been experiencing persistent or uncontrollable worry or anxiety about everyday things?

Um, no, not really. I don't feel anxious or worried about things. I mean, I have normal everyday stress, but it's not uncontrollable or anything like that. It's mostly just that I'm too tired to deal with my normal routine, but I'm not sitting around feeling anxious about it.
Did this exhaustion start around the time of a specific major life stress or significant change?

No, I don't think so. There hasn't been any big change or major stress lately. Things have been pretty normal... well, except for me feeling this exhausted all the time. But it didn't start after anything specific happened, it just kind of set in.
